Shares of IBM (IBM) currently trade at 19.9 times earnings, while the S&P 500 sits at 21.9. Investors buying at that multiple need to understand the underlying assets, and the company has recently changed its messaging. During the fiscal Q2 2025 call, executives focused on a running total of generative AI business that they defined as their book of business. The most recent presentation offered a different focal point. So what is management talking up instead?

IBM Now Talks Up Recurring Software Revenue

Executives are now framing the company around reliable, repeating software revenue. During the fiscal Q2 2026 call on July 22, 2026, the company noted that about 80% of its annual software revenue is recurring. This division accounts for nearly 45% of total revenue.

A year prior, leadership anchored its pitch to a different metric. During the fiscal Q2 2025 call, the company reported its generative AI book of business stood at over $7.5 billion since inception. That figure climbed from over $3 billion during the fiscal Q3 2024 call. Highlighting a rapidly growing cumulative total gave investors a straightforward view into AI demand.

Generative AI remains part of the conversation. Management noted on the latest call that the technology represented about 50% of quarterly Consulting signings. Yet the company has stopped emphasizing the cumulative tally.

Software Is IBM's Largest Source Of Revenue

The software unit brought in $30.0 billion in fiscal 2025, accounting for 44% of the company's revenue over that period. Sales in the division expanded by 10.6%, compared with a 1.8% growth rate for Consulting, which is the second-largest business segment.

The company also tracks annual recurring revenue. Executives placed that metric at $24.6 billion during the most recent call, representing an 8% increase from a year earlier.

The generative AI metric measured a different type of performance: a cumulative book of business since inception. It never reflected actual yearly sales, whereas recurring software revenue provides an annual baseline.

Is IBM's Turn To Software Good News For You?

This strategic pivot toward software presents a more reassuring than concerning picture for investors, though it comes with a catch. A baseline of repeating revenue offers more stability than a lifetime tally of generative AI business, and this reliable income anchors the largest division at the company.

The complication is that software is also where IBM missed expectations during fiscal Q2 2026. Software revenue grew 5% for the quarter, but its organic growth was flat. Executives noted that tens of large deals failed to close on time, and that about a third of those delayed contracts had finalized by the earnings call.

If Palantir Stock Looks Expensive, You Need To Read This

Shares of Palantir Technologies (PLTR) currently trade at 137.7 times its adjusted earnings over the past twelve months, a metric that adds stock-based pay back after tax. Paying that multiple for a single year of profit appears steep, yet the valuation shifts when measured against the next two years. The following breakdown highlights what investors are actually paying for the profit Palantir is expected to generate over those two years.

How Much You Pay For Palantir's Coming Earnings

Based on the consensus forecast for fiscal 2026, which concludes this December, Palantir trades at 121.5 times earnings. Looking further ahead to the forecast for fiscal 2027, the valuation falls to 81.7 times. Both figures offer a stark contrast to the 137.7 multiple applied to the past twelve months.

The share price remains constant across all three calculations, and only the underlying profit estimates change. Palantir earned $3.7 billion on that adjusted basis over the past twelve months. Projections call for the company to earn $4.1 billion in fiscal 2026 and $6.2 billion in fiscal 2027.

Palantir Has To Grow Revenue By Half

Hitting those targets requires Palantir to maintain rapid expansion, even if the pace slows from its current trajectory. The consensus forecast indicates sales will rise 50.2% from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2027, reaching $12.3 billion. Projected profit increases 48.6% on the same forecast, tracking almost in step with sales and assuming no wider margin between the two years.

Palantir is currently growing at a faster clip. Sales climbed 78.9% over the past twelve months, and rose 92.8% in the latest quarter compared to a year earlier. During the company's August 3, 2026 call, management noted immense demand from enterprises for sovereign AI.

The consensus sales forecast for fiscal 2026 aligns closely with internal guidance. Management used that same call to raise its full-year sales guidance to a range between $8.150 billion and $8.158 billion. The current forecast sits just 0.7% above the midpoint of that range.

Palantir Needs Fat Profits And One Market To Last

The profit margin represents the most likely area where Palantir could fall short of expectations. The consensus forecast models Palantir keeping 50% of its sales as net profit in fiscal 2026, compared to 43% in fiscal 2025, the last full year it reported. Palantir kept 49% of its sales as net profit over the past twelve months, so the forecast asks it to hold that level for a full year. Management also warned on the August call that it expected a significant ramp in expenses in the third quarter, because of the seasonal timing of new hires. That quarter has ended, and Palantir has not yet reported its results. Costs that rise faster than sales would bring the forecast profit down.

title: What Changed For HPE Stock, And What Did Not?
detail:
What Changed For HPE Stock, And What Did Not?
Trefis Team

Image from Pixabay

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) stock returned 193.4% in the year to October 12, 2026, far outpacing the 20.5% return for the S&P 500. The company's sales growth sped up over those twelve months, and management raised its outlook for fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 on September 2, 2026. On September 30, it raised its long-term growth forecast for its networking business and announced a $1.2 billion AI order from cloud firm Vultr. So how much has the business itself grown over that year?

How Quickly Is HPE's Revenue Rising?

Sales over the last twelve months reached $41.9 billion, up 26.6% from $33.1 billion a year earlier. Revenue in fiscal Q3 2026 reached a record $12.2 billion. That figure was up 34% from a year earlier, management noted during the September 2, 2026 call. Just three quarters before that, sales were growing 14.4%. Unlike the order figure below, these growth rates are not adjusted for the acquired Juniper Networks.

Server revenue grew 35% in fiscal Q3 2026. Management stated that higher selling prices on traditional servers drove the increase, while supply limits restricted the total number of servers HPE could ship. AI systems brought in almost $1.6 billion of that quarter's sales.

What Does HPE Stock Cost Against Its Sales Now?

HPE stock currently costs 2.2 times the company's sales over the last twelve months. That multiple had stayed between 0.4 and 1.4 over the past ten years. The share price rose far faster than sales did, so buyers now pay more for each dollar of HPE's revenue than they did in any of those years. On earnings, the stock is priced at 33.7 times.

The stock price appears to assume sales will keep growing, and management is forecasting exactly that. The company expects fiscal Q4 2026 revenue of $13.9 billion to $14.8 billion, which is above the record it reported for Q3. Management now expects revenue to grow 13% to 17% for fiscal 2027. Orders grew 42% in fiscal Q3 2026, calculated on a basis that counts the acquired Juniper Networks in both years. Furthermore, HPE ended the quarter with a record backlog.

HPE's Margin Is Back At 7.8%

HPE kept 7.8% of its sales as operating profit over the last twelve months. This matches the 7.8% it kept two years ago. The margin fell to 6.2% a year ago and has since recovered, yet it remains below the 8.8% recorded three years ago. It is also far below the 18.5% posted by the S&P 500.

Management stated on the September 2, 2026 call that it expects its adjusted operating margin, which runs well above the 7.8% figure, to decline from the previous quarter. The company named a larger share of AI systems in what it sells among the reasons for this expected drop. The adjusted operating margin is the number to watch when the company reports fiscal Q4 2026.

title: Arista Networks vs. International Business Machines: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Arista Networks vs. International Business Machines: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Jake Lerch, The Motley Fool
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 10:35 AM MDT 6 min read
ANET
IBM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Choosing between Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) and International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) in 2026 requires balancing high-octane infrastructure demand with stable, diversified software and consulting services amid an evolving technology landscape.

Arista Networks specializes in high-speed switches for massive data centers, while International Business Machines focuses on hybrid cloud and AI platforms. Both benefit from the artificial intelligence boom, but they offer different financial profiles. One is a high-growth hardware leader, whereas the other is a legacy giant undergoing a steady transformation.

The case for Arista Networks

Arista Networks designs networking products for cloud titans and enterprise data centers. Its focus on "Scale Up" and "Scale Out" networking helps customers meet the high data demands of artificial intelligence clusters. Large purchases by a limited number of customers continue to account for a substantial share of revenue, and such customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $9.0 billion, which was an increase of approximately 28.6% over the previous year. Net income for the period was close to $3.5 billion, representing a net margin of roughly 39%. This growth reflects strong demand for the company's 800G switching products in the tech stocks landscape.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x, indicating it holds no debt relative to its shareholder equity. The current ratio, which evaluates the ability to cover short-term debts with current assets, was a robust 3.0x. For FY 2025, free cash flow (the cash remaining after operations and capital investments) reached approximately $4.3 billion.

The case for International Business Machines

International Business Machines provides a mix of software, consulting, and infrastructure services with a heavy focus on hybrid cloud platforms. It often partners with other leaders, such as Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and SAP (NYSE:SAP), to facilitate digital transformations for global enterprises. In October 2026, the company launched a collaboration with Zscaler (NASDAQ:ZS)and its subsidiary, Red Hat, to modernize private application protection.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $67.5 billion, an increase of approximately 7.6% over the previous 12 months. Net income for the year was close to $10.6 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 15.7%. While its growth rate is lower than that of smaller networking firms, the massive scale of its consulting and software segments provides a diversified revenue base.

Accenture Stock Surges 60% in 3 Months: Is ACN Still a Buy?

Accenture ACN shares have surged 60% over the past three months, significantly outperforming the industry's 6% growth. The impressive rally reflects optimism surrounding the company's expanding artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities, strong enterprise relationships and digital transformation opportunities. However, following such substantial appreciation, investors must evaluate whether its earnings outlook and business fundamentals justify further upside.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Accenture's diversified service portfolio, strategic acquisitions and consistent cash generation support its long-term prospects. Nevertheless, restrained discretionary spending, pricing competition and modest organic revenue growth expectations suggest that investors should approach the stock cautiously.

ACN's Earnings Outlook Signals Gradual Improvement

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Accenture's first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings stands at $3.89 per share, indicating a 1.3% year-over-year decline. Revenues are projected at $19.35 billion, indicating 3.2% growth.

For fiscal 2027, the consensus earnings estimate of $14.68 per share suggests 5.1% year-over-year growth. Revenues are expected to increase 4.2% to $77.33 billion.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The outlook strengthens for fiscal 2028, with earnings projected to rise 8.2% to $15.88 per share and revenues anticipated to grow 4.7% to $80.95 billion. These estimates indicate steady business expansion, although the earnings trajectory may not fully support expectations of rapid growth following the stock's sharp rally.

Enterprise AI Adoption Expands ACN's Opportunities

Growing enterprise investment in AI, cloud modernization and data infrastructure continues to create opportunities for Accenture. Businesses increasingly require technology integration, process redesign and specialized expertise to deploy AI applications across operations.

In fiscal 2026, more than 400 clients initiated advanced AI engagements with Accenture. Revenues from its eight emerging AI and data partners more than doubled, while bookings more than tripled year over year.

The company's workforce of nearly 110,000 AI and data professionals strengthens its ability to execute complex transformation programs. Its extensive technology partnerships also support broader adoption of AI-driven solutions.

As organizations move toward enterprise-wide AI implementation, demand for consulting, integration and managed services could sustain long-term revenue opportunities.

When Palantir's CEO and the Chart Say the Same Thing, Pay Attention

Image from Pixabay

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance on August 3. The stock is up 69.8% since the preceding close, against 4.2% for the S&P 500. A higher forecast from management and a rising share price do not always arrive at the same time. A stock displaying both warrants a closer look. Here is the guidance Palantir raised, what the chart shows, and what could push the stock higher.

How Much Did Palantir Lift Its 2026 Forecast?

Management raised its revenue guide for fiscal 2026 to between $8.15 billion and $8.158 billion. The prior expectation was $7.66 billion. That amounts to 6.5% more than it forecast before for the same year. Management called this the largest full-year revenue guidance raise it has ever made. The revision moves a projection higher, rather than counting sales already made.

Management pointed to the U.S. business, where revenue grew 115% from a year earlier in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. On the same August 3 call, the company noted that businesses want sovereign AI.

The raise went beyond total revenue. Management lifted its guide for U.S. commercial revenue, which covers sales to businesses in the U.S., to more than $3.424 billion from $3.22 billion. Every other full-year line the company revised moved up as well, including adjusted free cash flow. Management guided no line lower.

Palantir Shares Are In A Rising Trend

Palantir stock sits above both averages that chart readers track. The shares closed at $209.00 on October 12, 2026. The shorter average, which measures the closing price over the last 50 trading days, stood at $178.70. The longer average, tracking the same measure over 200 trading days, stood at $152.41. A price above its shorter average, combined with a shorter average above the longer one, defines a rising trend.

The gain arrived in two parts. The stock rose 32.2% during the two sessions around the release, against 3.3% for the S&P 500. That move priced the quarter's results and the new guide together. Palantir has added another 28.5% since then, while the index gained 0.9%. A trend describes historical price action, and it is not a forecast of what comes next.

What Does Palantir Need From The Rest Of 2026?

Palantir can meet its raised guide even if growth slows from the first half of fiscal 2026. Two quarters of fiscal 2026 are still to be reported. The guide leaves about $4.6 billion of revenue for those periods. That translates to 77.2% growth over the same quarters last year, against 89.0% in the two quarters already reported.

title: What Did Dell Stock Investors Miss Before The Run?
detail:
What Did Dell Stock Investors Miss Before The Run?
Trefis Team
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:15 AM MDT 3 min read
DELL
^GSPC
HPQ
HPE
IBM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Shares of Dell Technologies (DELL) returned 274.5% in the twelve months to October 12, 2026, easily outpacing the 17.3% return for the S&P 500. That climb centered on servers, particularly the hardware Dell builds for artificial intelligence, along with related storage equipment. Investors who missed the rally might wonder if they could have anticipated it. How early did Dell's own reports show it?

Dell Had The Pipeline Well Before The Revenue

The earliest clear signal arrived during Dell's fiscal Q3 2025 earnings call, held on November 26, 2024. Executives posted revenue of $24.4 billion, representing a 10% increase, and credited the growth to the infrastructure group that sells servers and storage. They noted the sales pipeline for the next five quarters had expanded by more than 50% from the previous quarter across all customer categories.

Actual sales took longer to materialize. Revenue growth decelerated to 7.2% in fiscal Q4 2025 and slipped further to 5.1% in fiscal Q1 2026. By April 2025, the stock had lost 28% so far that year, a decline that a Motley Fool article attributed to tepid quarterly results and tariff worries.

Confirmation finally came with the fiscal Q2 2026 results, which executives discussed on an August 28, 2025 call before filing them on September 8, 2025. Revenue for that quarter reached $29.8 billion, rising 19.0% from a year earlier. That filing appeared a month before October 9, 2025, the start of the twelve months measured here. The market did not wait. The stock had already returned 99.6% in the six months before that date. The early signs were genuine. The stock had already roughly doubled in the six months to October 2025, and it then rose another 274.5% over the next twelve months.

Most Dell Revenue Now Comes From Servers And Storage

Dell's infrastructure group generated a record $31.8 billion in fiscal Q2 2027, reflecting an 89% increase. The company posted total revenue of $47 billion that quarter, meaning servers and storage made up about two-thirds of it. That single unit now books more sales in a quarter than the entire company managed when executives first highlighted the pipeline in November 2024.

Over the twelve months to October 12, 2026, Dell also heavily outperformed the two other hardware manufacturers: Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock returned 172.7%, and HP stock returned 16.4%.

Are Dell's AI Server Orders Still Building?

Yes, as of Dell's latest report. During the fiscal Q2 2027 call held on September 1, 2026, executives announced that Dell booked a record $60.9 billion of AI server orders in the quarter. The company recognized $16.4 billion of AI server revenue over those same three months. By the end of the quarter, the AI backlog of undelivered orders reached a record $95 billion.
